newsitem.title: UK: Sainsbury drops amid price war fears.
newsitem.headline: Sainsbury drops amid price war fears.

text.p: Shares in UK supermarket group J Sainsbury Plc extended Friday's tumble as market research group Verdict warned on Monday there was a high risk of a price war in the sector and amid negative press comment following the company's profit warning last week.
Sainsbury shares were down 7-1/2p at 333-1/2 by 0807 GMT after on Friday sliding 51p.
Among other food retailers, Tesco Plc was down 3-1/2p at 356-1/2, Safeway Plc was down 5-1/2p at 384 and ASDA Group Plc was down 1-1/2p at 120.

In a report on the supermarket sector, Verdict said Sainsbury needed to regain the initiative from market leader Tesco and might resort to price cutting if current policies failed to restore sales growth.
Verdict said Sainsbury would be most likely to start a price war, though Tesco could make a pre-emptive move if it thought Sainsbury was about to launch a new initiative.

Separately the influential Lex column in Saturday's Financial Times said their was "scant evidence" that Sainsbury's fortunes had bottomed out and the stock did not deserve to trade at the same price-earnings ratio as Tesco.
